newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel asks France to work for Lebanon pullout.
newsitem.headline: Israel asks France to work for Lebanon pullout.

text.p: Israel said on Friday it had asked France to help find a way to reach an accord that would allow Israeli troops to pull out of Lebanon.

Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai told Israel Radio: "I asked the French defence minister ... to use their influence on the Lebanese government and the Lebanese army to fight terrorism and search for ways in which we can reduce the violence and find solutions for Lebanon".
"I emphasised to my counterpart that we have no interest in one centimetre of Lebanese land," Mordechai said.

France, once colonial overlord in Lebanon, has periodically tried in talks with Syria, Lebanon, and Israel to negotiate an Israeli withdrawal from a south Lebanon occupation zone Israel patrols with South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia allies.

Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas regularly attack Israeli troops and the SLA to try to oust them from the 15 km (nine mile) -wide occupation zone set up in 1985 when Israel withdrew the bulk of its 1982 invasion forces.

Israel's newspaper Haaretz reported on Friday that about three months before the start of the 1982 invasion, a comprehensive wargame at Israel's military headquarters showed the chances Israel would achieve its strategic aims in war were slim. Haaretz said these conclusions were not presented to then-Prime Minister Menachem Begin or other cabinet ministers.

The 1982 invasion spearheaded by then-Defence Minister Ariel Sharon was the start of the most unpopular war in Israel. It aroused fierce opposition, even bloodshed. Ultimately about 650 Israelis and thousands of Arab civilians died in the Lebanon campaign that spread to Beirut.
